text: {"answer": "The evidence mostly supports a positive or neutral productivity effect of remote work, but with important conditions. Several sources report gains: a field experiment found remote working generally increased job performance, especially for mothers [ef88116f982d#1], and a Saudi financial-sector study found remote work raised productivity through job satisfaction and work-life balance [d3dba06e800d#2]. A meta-analysis summary reports a median +10% for focused tasks but -4% for collaborative tasks [d658dc380b73#5]. A randomized trial of hybrid schedules found no measurable productivity difference from in-office peers [d658dc380b73#5], and a managers' experiment found a two-day hybrid schedule does not damage performance [a5a6c6342091#2]. The contradicting side is real: a panel survey of 3,123 office workers found full-remote work (five days a week) was associated with reduced work productivity and increased presenteeism, though partial remote work reduced stress [abefd158b9c2#2][abefd158b9c2#0].
